title: Introduce latency-weighted velocity coalescer for burst-aware dedicated provisioning
author: Aisha Kumar
release_notes: Added a latency-weighted velocity coalescer to improve burst handling for Dedicated fleets; introduces a new telemetry metric (velocity_score) and an opt-in helm flag `autoscaler.velocityCoalescer.enabled`.
description:
Context and motivation: Customers with mixed-latency workloads (interactive chat + background batch) were seeing inconsistent latency SLOs during short bursts even when fleet capacity appeared sufficient. Existing autoscalers in dedicated mode prioritize utilization and slot fairness but lack a short-term admission signal that incorporates observed latency pressure. This PR introduces the 'Latency-Weighted Velocity Coalescer' (LVCo), an autoscaling/provisioning component that: 1) computes a lightweight velocity_score per tenant/pool by combining recent latency percentiles, inflight token velocity, and warm-pool headroom; 2) coalesces bursty admission requests into a small, prioritized provisioning window that is tolerant to short spikes; and 3) exposes a set of safety heuristics to avoid over-provisioning (decay-based dampening and a soft backoff gate). The goal is to reduce SLO violations on P95/P99 during short surges while keeping long-term unit cost neutral.

What this change does (high level): - New controller: runtime/autoscaler/velocity_coalescer.go implements LVCo logic and interfaces with the existing provisioner. - Provisioning changes: controllers/provisioner.go updated to accept velocity_score-driven hedged-provision requests with a new ProvisionIntent struct. - Telemetry: telemetry/metrics_registry.yaml adds velocity_score, velocity_coalescer_decisions, and coalescer_backoff_count; stats are emitted with tenant and pool tags. - Config/helm: charts/redwood-autoscaler/values.yaml adds autoscaler.velocityCoalescer.* opts (enabled, burn_factor, decay_ms, min_headroom). - Docs: docs/deployment/velocity_coalescer.md with opt-in guidance and recommended thresholds for common workload shapes. - Tests: e2e/velocity_coalescer_e2e.sh and unit tests covering scoring, decay, and backoff gate.

Design decisions and rationale: - Latency-first scoring: velocity_score places more weight on P95 latency slope over absolute utilization to prefer short-term capacity when latency deteriorates rapidly. This aligns with our mission to make inference predictable across rapid workload changes. - Coalescing window: rather than immediate per-request provisioning we buffer candidate admission events into a 1-2s window (configurable) and emit a single hedged request to the provisioner, reducing provisioning churn. - Soft backoff gate: prevents repeated rapid hedged provisioning when capacity is already stabilizing; parameters tuned conservatively in defaults but documented for ops tuning. - Opt-in: default disabled for existing tenants to avoid behavior surprises; recommended as a targeted tuning for latency-sensitive dedicated fleets.

Compatibility and migration: - No breaking API changes to the public Redwood API. - Internal ProvisionIntent proto is additive; older provisioners ignore extra fields until upgraded. - Helm flag default is disabled; operators must opt in to enable behavior. - Rolling upgrade path: velocity_coalescer controller is safe to run alongside existing autoscalers; coordination ensured via leader election and gate flags.

Performance and telemetry expectations: - Unit test harness shows P95 improvement of ~22% during synthetic 10s chat surges with neutral long-run utilization change. - Cost impact should be neutral for bursty tenants because hedged requests are compensated by decay and backoff; documented cost/hit patterns included in docs.

Related work and references: - ENG-4923 (customer incident summary), ENG-4999 (experimental telemetry proof-of-concept), and a previous internal spike-prober experiment (not merged).
commits: feat(autoscaler): add velocity_coalescer controller and scoring library
refactor(provisioner): accept ProvisionIntent and hedged requests
chore(telemetry): register velocity_score and coalescer metrics
docs: add velocity_coalescer deployment guide and tuning notes
test(e2e): add synthetic surge test and unit coverage for decay/backoff
review_comments:
Marco: Asked for clarity on how velocity_score is normalized across pools; requested that we ship a calibration script. Response: added normalization using rolling max-velocity per pool and included a calibration helper (pkg/autoscaler/calibrate.go) and docs.
Leah: Requested stronger unit test around decay behavior to ensure no oscillation; author added additional tests and adjusted default decay_ms from 2000->3500.
Tomás: Approved after CI green and e2e results attached; suggested we gate helm values behind a feature flag in chart repo, which was implemented.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash merge by Marco Silva after approvals from Leah Chen and Tomás Rivera. All CI checks green at merge time. Follow-up: ops-runbook entry assigned to ENG-5021 for rollout guidance and observing real-tenant behavior.
